newsitem.title: USA: More subpoenas in U.S. political contributions case.
newsitem.headline: More subpoenas in U.S. political contributions case.

text.p: A Justice Department task force has issued subpoenas to more than 40 people and businesses in its probe of alleged illegal foreign campaign contributions to Democrats, party sources said Monday.

The subpoenas, issued through a federal grand jury, were first reported in USA Today, which said it based its information on a "confidential" Democratic Party document it obtained that was prepared by Democratic National Committee (DNC) general counsel Joseph Sandler. Sandler had asked DNC employees to thoroughly search their files and not alter any documents.
Democratic sources confirmed that subpoenas had been issued.
Earlier subpoenas were issued for records at the White House and President Clinton's legal defence fund.

The newspaper said that among those subpoenaed were John Huang, a naturalised American of Chinese descent who was a Commerce Department official before becoming a top Democratic Party fundraiser, and John Berry of Little Rock, Arkansas, a long time friend of Clinton.
Berry denied to USA Today that he ever raised funds from foreign corporations or individuals.

Huang is at the centre of investigations by a 25-agent FBI task force and congressional committees into several million dollars in contributions he solicited, much of it from Asian Americans or allegedly from foreigners or people with foreign business ties.
He is a former executive of the Lippo Group, a financial conglomerate based in Indonesia.
It is illegal for non-Americans to make political contributions in most cases unless people are legal residents of this country.
After a furore broke during the presidential campaign about improper contributions, the DNC voluntarily returned money it deemed inappropriate or illegal.
DNC spokeswoman Amy Weiss Tobe refused comment. "We don't comment on subpoenas. We are cooperating with any and all aspects in investigations," she said.
